title: Pointer arithmetic past array bound in checksum loop
rule_text: Do not form or use out-of-bounds pointers or array subscripts
context: Flagged because the loop condition uses `<=` instead of `<`, which reads one byte past the end of `buf` on the final iteration. Please confirm whether `len` is ever passed as `buf`'s allocated size minus one elsewhere in the caller (which would make this intentional but still fragile), or whether this is a straightforward off-by-one.

title: Dereference of possibly-NULL return from malloc before check
context: `malloc` result for `c` is dereferenced immediately on the next line with no NULL check. Also note `c->data` (the second malloc) is never checked either. Flag both or just the first, whichever is more useful for the human's comment.

title: Freed buffer pointer reused after error path in parser
rule_text: Free dynamically allocated memory when no longer needed
context: This one actually looks fine on a first read — scratch is freed on both the early-return path and the normal path, and there's no use-after-free that I can find. Flagging as a candidate false positive; the static pass matched on "malloc without free in this function's immediate scope" but missed the early-return free. Please double check the `validate()` call doesn't stash a copy of the pointer somewhere though — I didn't have visibility into that function's body.

title: Fixed-size stack buffer filled by strcpy from untrusted input
rule_text: Guarantee that storage for strings has sufficient space for character data and the null terminator
context: `raw` comes from an HTTP request header parsed a few functions up the call stack; I could not confirm whether it's length-capped before reaching this function — the parsing code lives in a different translation unit (`http_parse.c`) that wasn't included in this review batch. Marking needs-more-context rather than a hard violation call until someone can check the caller chain. If it turns out `raw` is unbounded, this is a straightforward stack buffer overflow (strcpy has no bounds check against `value`'s 32-byte size).
